issues.description: Exercise 1 requires the simulate() function to "return the statevector" (problem statement), but the template's simulate() method is annotated to return list[complex] while the solution returns the statevector object produced by Qiskit (result.get_statevector), which is a Statevector/ndarray rather than a Python list[complex]. This mismatch between the annotated/expected return type and the actual returned object can confuse students (type expectations, tests, or suggested post-processing) and may cause static type checks or example code to be inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the template method annotation and documentation to expect and document a Qiskit Statevector/np.ndarray (e.g. -> Statevector | np.ndarray) and show example usage, or (B) have the solution convert the simulator output explicitly to a list of complex (e.g. output_state = result.get_statevector(...).data.tolist()) before returning so it matches the template annotation. Update the problem statement to state the precise expected Python type (Statevector, numpy array, or list[complex]).
